Dwight sank back on his heels, finally letting the tension leave his shoulders. His hands were trembling — still streaked with dust and blood — and he balled them tightly against his lap trying to steady himself. Felix reached for his neck, fingers searching for his pulse — and David flinched hard, jerking back with a hitched breath as his eyes flew open. Alarm flickered there for a split second, chased quickly by confusion... then heat. Embarrassed fury, sharp and defensive. He shoved Felix’s hand away with a clumsy swat, the effort barely coordinated. “‘m fine,” he wheezed — the words cracked, shredded, broken in half by another coughing fit. His body twitched as he dragged in a breath, followed by another, each one a battle. Still, he braced a hand beneath himself, stubborn to a fault, trying to push upright even as his whole frame trembled from the strain. Felix didn’t even wait for him to finish coughing before the fury hit. “You idiot,” he snapped, voice tight and sharp with leftover panic. “ How long were you having trouble breathing in there? Why didn’t you say anything?! I would have changed the entire approach! You damn near got yourself killed! What the hell were you thinking?!” David, still catching up to the reality of being not dead , didn’t flinch. His legs shook under him, right arm cradled close, but his jaw locked stubbornly as he shoved himself up another inch. “We don’t have time for this,” he growled, eyes lit with a glare so sharp it looked like he planned to punch the Fog itself into submission. He staggered to his feet like a man with something to prove, wobbly legs carrying him limping towards the nearest doorway. Dwight scrambled to steady him, reaching an arm out — but David batted him away, stubbornly dragging one foot past the other in a crooked shuffle toward the edge of the Eyrie. “ Unbelievable, ” Dwight muttered, half to himself. Watching the man push forward on half a lung, a jacked-up arm, and the raw fuel of unprocessed rage, he couldn’t help the breathless laugh that broke loose. “Stubbornness and pure spite. That’s all he’s running on.” The universe seemed to agree. As if on cue, David’s eyes rolled back mid-step, knees buckling, his body finally cashing the debt his bravado had racked up. Dwight caught him just in time, locking his good arm around David’s shoulders. “Whoa — gotcha, gotcha—!” Felix moved in without a word, and together they got him back onto the sand, David groaning and muttering curses as they lowered him. He tried to fight it, but even the fight had gone soft now—just slurred protest and shallow breath. He was done. Felix leaned in close, his voice low, taut with fury still burning under the relief. “ Stay down , idiot. Don’t you ever do that to me again. Do you hear me?” His hands were firm against David’s shoulders, grounding and unrelenting. “You think you’re invincible, but I damn near just watched you die . I am not doing that again.” David blinked up at him, bleary and barely present. The words hit somewhere behind his eyes, too close and too loud, but he didn’t have the strength to push them away. The last thing he heard before the black overtook him was Felix’s voice — sharp, scolding, and laced with something bitter underneath that bloomed a fuzzy sense of guilt somewhere in the back of his mind. Ch 5 – Fallout The fire crackled low, casting warped shadows against the crumbling stone around camp. Soft amber light edged the survivors in flickers of warmth—on cloth, on skin, on all the things they weren’t saying. Dwight sat with his back to one of the ruined archways, his arm cradled in a makeshift sling — someone’s spare flannel, frayed at the edges. Not pain, exactly. What ache had survived the trip through the Fog had since settled into a dull stiffness that made every motion feel like a negotiation. Jill crouched by the fire, half-watching the embers, half-glaring at the others like she couldn’t decide whether to scold them or just throw a stick and call it even. "I leave for one trial," she muttered, breaking the silence. "And you clowns manage to trigger a cave-in? What the hell even happened in there?" Dwight opened his mouth. Closed it again. Thought better of the whole idea. The tension was high enough, and he didn’t feel like having it turn against him. The fire held its breath. Crackled, but barely. Its glow pushed shadows into the corners of the old stone ring, gilding faces that weren’t looking at each other, only at the flicker between them. Across the flames, Felix sat on the bare stone — not quite hunched, but folded tight. Hands limp in his lap. Legs pulled in close. Coiled, like movement would be too much. Like stillness was the only way to stop everything from slipping sideways. The firelight glinted off his face in brief, uneven flashes — too bright, too sharp. His gaze stayed fixed on the flames, but there was nothing soft about it. Quiet fury, bottled perfectly behind his eyes. David sat opposite him. Slouched, smaller than usual, shoulders drawn in like a man trying to disappear into the earth one vertebra at a time. His jacket was off, tossed somewhere behind him. Shirt sleeves shoved up to the elbows, exposing the bruises that tracked his arm in raw, splotchy streaks — violet and wine-dark, angry even in the Fog’s forgiving light. He’d barely said two words since his second impromptu nap. Claudette had checked his ribs with gentle fingers. Meg had given him a mug of something warm and vaguely sweet.
